articles.title: No more Kumbh traffic woes! Prayagraj's new 9.8-km Ganga bridge is opening in November — and it could change the city forever

articles.title: Payday winners: India’s salary hikes projected at 8.6%-10.2%; who gets the most?
articles.summary: Professionals in electric vehicles, fintech, healthcare, and engineering can expect brighter salary outlooks. Fast-growing sectors and technical roles will likely see higher pay increases.

articles.title: 1854 to today: The mountain school where history meets global education
articles.summary: Founded in 1854, Woodstock School in Mussoorie is one of India’s oldest international boarding schools, known for its Himalayan campus, heritage architecture and global education.

articles.summary: TV actress Saumya Tandon’s Mumbai home reflects her personal style with vintage European interiors, pastel shades, classic furniture and artistic corners designed without a professional decorator.

articles.title: TVS’ big move for kids: This mini bike could create India’s next racing stars
articles.summary: TVS Racing’s Apache RR 200 Mini brings professional-style racing to young riders aged 10-14. With a 197.75cc engine and track-focused setup, it aims to create India’s future racers.

articles.title: Machine failed, business suffered: Kerala entrepreneur wins ₹75,000 after three-year battle over ₹25 lakh equipment

articles.summary: iPhone 18 Pro leaks point to a 2nm A20 Pro chip, 5,500 mAh battery, 35% smaller Dynamic Island, Dark Cherry colour and manual camera aperture — starting at ₹1,39,900 in India.

articles.summary: Namo Bharat adds 52 extra daily trips on the Delhi-Meerut corridor ahead of Kanwar Yatra rush. Trains will run every 8 minutes to ease travel for commuters and pilgrims.

articles.title: Higher US LPG imports: Why Indian Oil is looking to acquire 50% stake in very large gas carriers
articles.summary: If the plan goes ahead, IOC will become the first Indian refiner to own VLGCs. At present, the company primarily depends on time-chartered vessels to transport both LPG and crude oil.

articles.title: Your UPI app now works for Dubai’s Burj Khalifa tickets — here’s what Indian travellers need to know

articles.summary: Gurgaon Metro's new line will directly connect with Delhi Metro's Yellow Line at Millennium City Centre via platform and concourse-level access — minimising walking distance for commuters.

articles.title: South Korea's Kospi tumbles 6% as SK Hynix slide, AI spending worries trigger chip selloff
articles.summary: South Korea's Kospi index dropped significantly due to chipmaker weakness. SK Hynix reported earnings that missed market expectations, causing its shares to fall. This selloff reflects investor concerns over high valuations for artificial intelligence-linked stocks.

articles.title: Indian IT stocks rally: Why TCS, Infosys, Wipro are rising as global AI stocks plunge
articles.summary: The gains came even as India's IT sector continues to face headwinds, including subdued discretionary technology spending, pricing pressure, higher employee costs and uncertainty over how artificial intelligence could affect conventional outsourcing revenues.

articles.title: Why Johnson & Johnson agreed to pay $5.5 billion despite denying cancer claims
articles.summary: J&J said it expects to pay $3 billion in 2027, with further payments in 2028, though the total value could rise depending on how many people join the settlement.

articles.title: How India’s IT giants are reinventing themselves for the AI era
articles.summary: As AI reshapes outsourcing and clients shift work to GCCs, companies such as TCS and HCLTech are expanding into data centres and GCC-as-a-service to tap a larger share of AI spending.

articles.summary: The Delhi-Pune flight SG 939 was first delayed due to a technical issue and later cancelled, leaving more than 180 travellers stranded inside the airport for over six hours.

articles.summary: ABP owns and operates 21 ports across England, Scotland and Wales, including Immingham, the UK's largest port by tonnage, and Southampton, the leading export port handling £40 billion worth of exports annually.

articles.title: 100% tariffs for India? US Senate advances key Russian sanctions bill
articles.summary: The US Senate overwhelmingly advanced a bipartisan bill to impose new sanctions on Russia. This legislation grants President Trump powers to penalize major energy export buyers. India and China are among the largest customers of Russian crude oil and natural gas.

articles.title: Gold, silver prices slip as Fed decision, stronger dollar keep traders cautious
Crude prices climb over 4% as Middle East tensions, inventory draw fuel supply fears
articles.summary: Oil prices rebounded sharply on Wednesday due to renewed Middle East tensions. Concerns over global crude supplies and lower US inventories supported the market. Military developments in the region and air strikes on militant targets heightened worries.

articles.title: Radico Khaitan sees 10% jump in revenue
articles.summary: Radico Khaitan reported a 76% net profit increase for the June quarter. This growth was driven by strong demand for premium liquor brands. Easing input costs also contributed to the company's improved financial performance. Total income rose by 10% to Rs 5,869 crore.

articles.title: Delhi high court orders winding up of Paytm Payments Bank
articles.summary: The Delhi High Court has ordered the winding up of Paytm Payments Bank. This directive follows the Reserve Bank of India's cancellation of its banking license. The court appointed Girikumar M Nair as the official liquidator for this process.

articles.title: 'Transformation of Air India may take up to a decade'
articles.summary: Air India's transformation journey is now a decade-long endeavor. Supply chain disruptions and legacy system overhauls present significant challenges. The aviation industry faces constant pressures from global conflicts and fuel costs.

articles.title: Priceless stake: Noel's children now Tata Sons shareholders
articles.summary: Noel Tata's three children are now Tata Sons shareholders after inheriting shares. They each received two Tata Sons shares from their grandmother, Simone Tata. Simone Tata held eight shares before her passing in December 2025.

articles.title: Bad debt of PSBs at lowest levels in many decades: Government
articles.summary: Public sector banks report significant financial improvements and record profits. Bad debt levels have fallen to their lowest point in decades. The government has supported banks through capital infusions and legislative measures.

articles.title: As inflation bites, HUL to take more price hikes
articles.summary: Hindustan Unilever anticipates further price increases in coming months due to volatile commodity costs. The company projects inflation to remain between two and five percent for the September quarter.
